title: Access Provisioning and Spend Journeys (Company Playbook)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook centralizes company-wide routines for: access and permissions, change control, data handling, procurement and expense requests, vendor onboarding, and travel approvals. It is intended for requestors, approvers, finance, security, and operations teams.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors that require systems access, make purchases on behalf of Redwood, or manage configuration changes to production or corporate systems. Exceptions must be approved by Finance + Security.

Principles (short)
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required.
- Clear ownership: every access/expense/change has a named owner.
- Auditability: decisions and artifacts are retained for 3 years (longer for regulated customers).
- Separation of duties: requester ≠ approver for material spend and production changes.
- Risk-based controls: higher-risk assets require additional validation.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Requestor: submits request with business justification and expiry.
- Approver: validates business need and policy compliance.
- Provisioner: implements the access, change or purchase. For infra changes, this is the engineering owner.
- Finance: validates budget and PO requirement for purchases > $5,000.
- Security: performs risk review for access to sensitive assets (PCI/PHI/Customer PII).
- Vendor Ops: manages supplier onboarding and contract records.

1) Access & Permissions: request-to-provision workflow
A. Access categories
- Standard internal apps: Google Workspace, Slack, Okta-managed SSO apps.
- Sensitive systems: production clusters, customer data stores, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
- Service accounts and API keys

B. Request flow (numbered steps)
1. Requestor fills the Access Request form in the internal portal. Required fields: owner, justification, asset identifier (service name), role, required duration, and risk notes.
2. Automated validation: system checks manager alignment, existing approvals, and if request touches sensitive assets.
3. Approver(s) notified: manager for standard access; manager + security for sensitive. Approvals are timeboxed to 48 hours.
4. Provisioner executes via IaC or identity provider. Provisioning must include an audit tag: "provisioned_by=<engineer>" and expiry metadata.
5. Post-provision review: owner confirms least-privilege within 7 days.
6. Revocation: requests with duration automatically expire; ad-hoc revocations are processed within 4 business hours for sensitive assets.

C. Example Access Request JSON (for integration):
{
  "request_id": "REQ-2026-0123",
  "requestor": "alice@example.com",
  "asset": "redwood-prod-cluster-3",
  "role": "read-only",
  "justification": "Support ticket #45121 - debug customer issue",
  "expiry": "2026-03-31"
}

D. Minimum approval matrix (table as text)
- Manager approval: any standard internal app.
- Manager + Security: access to customer data, KMS, or production write access.
- Manager + Security + Infra Eng lead: service accounts, long-lived keys (>90 days), or configuration write for core infra.

E. Access reviews
- Quarterly automated recertification for all roles.
- Monthly manual review for owners of assets classified high or critical.

2) Change Management (applies to infra and critical apps)
A. Change types
- Routine (low risk): config changes with no customer impact.
- Standard (planned): scheduled deploys within existing CI/CD gates.
- Emergency: rollbacks or fixes for live incidents.

B. Change lifecycle (numbered)
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) in the change tracker. Include: impact statement, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, and approver list.
2. Risk assessment: automated scoring based on affected services, blast radius, and user counts. Score > 7 requires Security + SRE signoff.
3. Approval: standard changes require SRE or owning eng manager; high-risk changes require cross-team approval and a canary plan.
4. Execution: operator runs the change following the runbook (include CLI snippets or playbook links).
5. Post-deploy verification: health checks and metric baselines for 60 minutes; if deviations exceed thresholds (5% traffic error rate increase or 30% latency tail degradation), initiate rollback.
6. Post-change review: update CR with lessons learned within 3 business days.

C. Emergency changes
- Emergency changes may bypass normal lead times but must be documented in the tracker within 24 hours and reviewed by the incident review board within 72 hours.

3) Data Management (classification & retention)
A. Classification levels
- Public: safe to publish externally.
- Internal: company-only, low sensitivity.
- Confidential: product roadmaps, non-public contracts.
- Restricted: customer PII/PHI, payment data — requires encryption at rest, access controls, audit logs.

B. Retention & deletion
- Default retention: documents and logs - 3 years.
- Customer PII/PHI: retention per contract or legal requirement; ensure secure deletion procedures and certs of destruction.

C. Data handling rules
- No customer data in personal devices or uncontrolled cloud storage.
- Use approved S3 buckets with encryption-and-logging policy for backups.

4) Procurement & Expenses
A. Purchase thresholds and approvals (table as text)
- <= $500: Manager approval.
- $501–$5,000: Manager + Finance cost center approval.
- > $5,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement (PO required).
- > $50,000: Procurement lead + Legal + Finance (contract & SLAs required).

B. Request-to-purchase flow (numbered)
1. Submit Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement portal with business justification, vendor, estimated cost, and budget code.
2. Finance validates budget availability within 2 business days.
3. Procurement reviews vendor terms and recommends PO or contract.
4. Once approved, Procurement issues a PO and Finance arranges payment terms.

C. Expense reporting and travel
- All expenses recorded within 10 business days of transaction. Receipts required for any expense > $25.
- Corporate card use: allowed for approved subscriptions and travel only. Disputes to be raised within 30 days.

5) Vendor Management
A. Onboarding checklist (numbered)
1. Vendor risk classification (low/medium/high) based on access and data processing.
2. Security questionnaire and evidence collection (SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports as relevant).
3. Contract template with data handling and breach notification clauses; Legal review required for high-risk vendors.
4. Technical integration: restrict network access to least-privilege IP ranges, short-lived credentials, and dedicated service accounts where possible.
5. SLA & monitoring: define uptime, support channels, escalation points, and regular review cadence.

B. Offboarding
- Revoke all credentials, confirm return or destruction of data, and archive contract artifacts. Vendor Ops must complete offboarding checklist within 5 business days.

6) Travel Policy (brief)
- Approvals: Manager pre-approval required for any travel. Trips with reimbursement > $2,000 require Finance pre-approval.
- Per-diem & limits: domestic hotel limit $250/night; international evaluated per region (Finance provides country caps).
- Booking: use corporate travel vendor where available; exceptions require manager justification.

7) Templates & Forms (links and examples)
- Access Request Form: internal portal link (use template ID: ARF-2025).
- Purchase Request Template: include vendor, justification, budget code, and anticipated SOW.
- Change Request Template: include test plan, rollback, and impact matrix.
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: checklist with required evidence fields.

8) Escalation & Audit
- Escalate unresolved approval delays > 72 hours to the team director.
- Security incidents involving vendor or data must follow the Incident Response policy and be reported to Security Pager within 1 hour.
- Audit cadence: internal audit team runs an annual review; targeted audits occur after significant incidents.

9) Metrics & KPIs to monitor
- Time-to-provision (median target: 24 hours for standard apps).
- Time-to-approve purchases (median target: 3 business days).
- Quarterly access recertification completion rate (target: 95%).
- Number of emergency changes and post-change rollback rate (target rollback < 5%).

Appendices
A. Example CLI snippet to revoke an API key (for infra owners)
$ redwoodctl keys revoke --key-id=svc-abc-123 --reason="project-complete"

B. Sample approval language (copy-paste for approvers)
"I approve this request as the owner/manager. I confirm budget and business justification, and I understand the access will expire on the date specified."

C. Frequently Asked Questions (short)
Q: Who to contact for fast-track access?
A: Managers may request an expedited path; security must approve for sensitive assets. Fast-track is intended only for critical customer-impact scenarios.

D. Change history
- 2025-03-02: Playbook created (Asha Patel).
- 2025-10-15: Added vendor onboarding checklist (Priya Desai).
- 2026-02-14: Updated thresholds and revocation SLAs (Liam Torres).
